small_guidance:
- The conv (nn.Conv2d on 128×64×128×128 with k=3, out=128) is now the dominant cost — the instance-norm kernel is only a small tail. Add larger BLOCK configs (e.g. 32768) and try num_warps=4 for the small HW=126×126=15876 case which fits well under one large block (a single-pass persistent variant where BLOCK ≥ HW would eliminate the second load).
- Convert the IN kernel into a single-pass persistent version: when BLOCK ≥ HW (15876), load once, compute mean/var, then store — avoids re-reading from HBM.
- These tweaks will save maybe 0.1ms; they won't move fast_p meaningfully while conv dominates.
large_guidance:
- Replace nn.Conv2d with a custom Triton im2col-style GEMM kernel: one program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile), with implicit im2col gather. Shapes are OC=128, IC*kh*kw=64*9=576, output spatial=126*126=15876, batch=128 → very GEMM-friendly. Start with BLOCK_M=64 (OC), BLOCK_N=128 (spatial), BLOCK_K=32, num_warps=4, num_stages=3, autotuned.
- Fuse the instance-norm + divide epilogue into the conv kernel: have the conv kernel write per-(N,C) partial sum and sum-of-squares to scratch (atomic-add or per-program reduce), then a second small kernel computes mean/rstd and a third applies the affine. Or: do a two-pass approach where conv writes output normally, then the existing IN kernel fuses. Bigger win is replacing the conv itself.
- Use channels_last (NHWC) layout so the K dimension (IC*kh*kw) gathers contiguously across IC. Hoist stride/pad index math out of the K loop. Mask spatial tail rather than branching.
